questions.q: In one sentence, what does CALCULATE do?
options: Sums every numeric column in a table automatically
Converts a calculated column into a measure
Evaluates an expression inside a modified filter context
Removes all relationships from a model temporarily
questions.explain: CALCULATE takes an expression (usually a measure or aggregation) and evaluates it after applying one or more filter arguments that modify the filter context.

questions.q: What happens if you call CALCULATE with only an expression and no filter arguments?
options: It returns blank in every case
It throws a syntax error — filters are required
It removes all existing filters automatically
It behaves exactly like the expression on its own
questions.explain: Filters are optional. With none supplied, CALCULATE simply evaluates the expression under the filter context that already exists.

questions.q: If a column already has a filter applied (e.g. from a slicer) and CALCULATE adds a new filter on that same column, what happens by default?
options: CALCULATE's filter is ignored in favor of the existing one
The two filters combine with AND logic automatically
Power BI throws an error for conflicting filters
CALCULATE's filter overwrites the existing one for that expression
questions.explain: By default, CALCULATE's filter argument replaces any existing filter on the same column — it doesn't combine with it. KEEPFILTERS changes this behavior.

questions.q: Besides a simple Boolean comparison, what else can a CALCULATE filter argument be?
options: A Power Query step
A table expression (like FILTER) or a filter modifier function (like ALL or REMOVEFILTERS)
Only a single column name with no condition
A visual formatting setting
questions.explain: CALCULATE accepts Boolean expressions, table expressions built with functions like FILTER, and filter modifier functions like ALL, ALLEXCEPT, or REMOVEFILTERS.

questions.q: Why is CALCULATE described as the most important function in DAX?
options: Nearly every advanced DAX pattern — percent of total, year-over-year growth, security filters — is built using it
It's the only function capable of aggregating a column
It's the fastest-executing function in the language
It's required in every single DAX formula, even the simplest ones
questions.explain: CALCULATE underlies most sophisticated DAX calculations by giving formulas a way to deliberately modify filter context — which is why it recurs constantly throughout the rest of this chapter.
